risk_catalogue.risk_details: Inclusion or presence of personal identifiable information (PII) and sensitive personal information (SPI) in the data used for training or fine tuning the model might result in unwanted disclosure of that information.
Confidential information might be included as part of the data that is used to train or tune the model.

A type of adversarial attack where an adversary or malicious insider injects intentionally corrupted, false, misleading, or incorrect samples into the training or fine-tuning datasets. An attacker manipulates development elements (the engineering environment and the supply chain), to alter the behavior of the model.

An extraction attack is used to create a shadow model of the original model. These attack occurs when an attacker is able to querie the original model to collect a sufficient number of outputs to create the shadow model that mimics the behaviour.
An attacker collects inputs and outputs of an existing model and uses those combinations to train a new model, in order to replicate the original model.

Evasion attacks attempt to make a model output incorrect results by slightly perturbing the input data that is sent to the trained model. An attacker fools the model by crafting input to mislead it into performing its task incorrectly

"Recent advances have shown that a deep learning model with high predictive accuracy frequently misbehaves on adversarial examples [57,58]. In particular, a small perturbation to an input image, which is imperceptible to humans, could fool a well-trained deep learning model into making completely different predictions [23]."
Most LLMs are developed using the Python language, whereas the vulnerabilities of Python interpreters pose threats to the developed models
Various Python libraries are used to create AI models. Vulnerabilities in these can affect the integrity of training data, AI models and deployment platforms.
"The software development toolchain of AI models is complex and could bring threats to the developed models." This results in the possibility of unrecognised malicious layers in a model,

Pre-processing tools play a crucial role in the context of LLMs. These tools, which are often involved in computer vision (CV) tasks, are susceptible to attacks that exploit vulnerabilities in tools such as OpenCV.

Data breaches occur from unauthorized access to data stored in the cloud. There are consequences of such breaches, which may range from financial damages and losses, legal ramifications to even reputational damage. Furthermore, configuration errors in cloud security, credential compromises, and vulnerable applications are some of the common causes of data breaches. At least 80% of data breaches in 2023 were due to data stored in the cloud, making the cloud a vulnerable segment. The tangible impacts of such a breach normally have long-lasting effects, which also include loss of customer confidence and lost revenue.

Most of the significant factors that cause cloud security breaches usually revolve around misconfiguration. Poor configuration settings, open storage buckets, overly permissive IAM policies, and publicly exposed resources containing sensitive data will expose critical information to attackers. Recently, it was reported that about 15% of cybersecurity breaches have been caused by cloud misconfigurations. This pinpoints a dire need for periodic audits of configurations made within the cloud to avoid exposure.

APIs are important for cloud functionality, and an unsecured API can be a reason for other security vulnerabilities. Insecure APIs generally have weak authentication, encryption, or validation, which hackers may then exploit in order to gain access to valuable cloud resources or to change data control. A staggering 92% of organizations experienced an API-related security incident in the past year. API vulnerabilities tend to go under the radar most times, hence a favorite target of attackers.

Data saved on the cloud can be lost via accidental deletion, hardware failures, and other types of malicious attacks. The lack of backup and disaster recovery puts most organizations in the line of risk of losing their valuable data permanently. Ransomware attacks are another leading cause of data loss, as they lock critical files with encryption and hold them for ransom.

In cloud computing, security operates on a shared responsibility model. While cloud providers are responsible for securing the infrastructure, organizations are supposed to secure their data, applications, and configurations. Most businesses don’t fully understand this model and, therefore, leave certain areas with gaps in security coverage. Organizations have to be conscious of their responsibilities to avoid leaving critical assets vulnerable.

Encryption is a part of protection for sensitive data that is stored in cloud environments or data in transit. Information that does not have strong encryption becomes easy prey for interception or access by those not authorized. Businesses that fail to encrypt sensitive information expose it to breach risks and non-compliance with privacy regulations.

Poor IAM practices, such as weak password policies or granting undue permission, can leave cloud resources open to unauthorized access. Such IAM misconfigurations pave the way for account compromises and data breaches. In addition, regular reviews of IAM policies and their respective MFA enforcement need to be performed to minimize the risk of unauthorized access.

Shadow IT refers to employees using unauthorized cloud applications or services without approval. This circumvents established security protocols, introducing risks and compliance issues. Shadow IT could result in data flows that are not monitored with possible data leaks, further increasing the attack surface for an organization. Implementing strict policies and monitoring tools can help mitigate the risks posed by Shadow IT.

While gaining much momentum in cloud environments, containers also introduce their own sets of security vulnerabilities if configured poorly. A container that is not properly configured or insecure communication between containers may expose the system to various kinds of attacks. There also should be a need for regular updates and security patches to minimize the danger of vulnerabilities in containerized environments.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall protect cloud assets against malware through deployment, activation and continuous monitoring of anti-malware mechanisms with automatic notification of detected threats.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall ensure that anti-malware protections are deployed, active and continuously monitored on every Virtual Machine, with: (i) protection enabled at all times, (ii) the number of detected threats reported as zero outside of incident windows, and (iii) automatic notification (e.g. email) of malware events through a logging service. This requirement supports continuous monitoring as defined in EUCS.

groups.title: OPS-07 Data Backup and Recovery – Monitoring

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall ensure that backup mechanisms are enabled, configured with adequate retention periods and continuously monitored for cloud-managed storage assets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall enable automated backup on every Storage asset and configure a retention period of at least 35 days. The backup configuration shall be continuously verified through monitoring.

groups.title: OPS-13 Logging and Monitoring – Identification of Events

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall enable comprehensive logging and monitoring across cloud assets to identify security-relevant events, including anomaly detection, with retention and integrity protection of logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall enable: (a) anomaly detection on Network Services; (b) activity, application, boot and operating-system logging on Virtual Machines; (c) a minimum log retention of 7 days for boot and OS logs; and (d) immutable storage of boot logs to protect log integrity.

groups.title: OPS-18 Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors – Online Registers

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall manage vulnerabilities by tracking online vulnerability registers and applying timely automatic updates to cloud assets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall enable automatic updates on every Virtual Machine and configure the update interval to at most 7 days, in line with the published online vulnerability registers.

groups.title: OPS-21 Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors – System Hardening

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall enforce system-hardening configurations on cloud-deployed assets, covering encryption at rest, encrypted transport, application firewalling and network-layer access restrictions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall enforce hardening on cloud assets, including: (a) state-of-the-art TLS (>=1.2) on Network Services; (b) Web Application Firewall enabled on Load Balancers; (c) encryption at rest on Storage assets; (d) encrypted backups on Storage; and (e) Layer-3 firewall enabled on Storage Services.

groups.title: CKM-02 Encryption of Data in Transit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall protect data in transit using state-of-the-art transport-layer encryption between cloud assets and clients, with progressively stricter enforcement at higher assurance levels.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall ensure that Storage Service HTTP endpoints accept encrypted connections using state-of-the-art transport-layer protocols.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CSP shall enforce that Storage Service HTTP endpoints reject unencrypted connections, requiring transport-layer encryption for all data exchanged.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system shall mitigate evasion and adversarial input attacks by augmenting training data and randomising input transformations to reduce model attack surface.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement data augmentation and randomisation techniques on the model inputs and/or training pipeline.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system shall filter and validate inputs sent to the AI model to detect and reject invalid, malformed or adversarially crafted samples.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement input filtering of invalid data at the API gateway and validation/sanitization at the data ingestion layer.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system shall detect adversarial queries and inputs targeting the AI model.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall deploy adversarial detection mechanisms (incl. adversarial training, input distortion, anomaly identification) at inference and at training time.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system shall protect against training-data poisoning by detecting and rejecting suspicious or anomalous samples and validating model behaviour.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement data validation/sanitisation, anomaly identification, model validation, data quality monitoring and ensemble/augmentation defences against poisoning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The cloud platform shall provide secure virtualization on Virtual Machines, including malware protection and event logging.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall enable malware protection and activity/application/boot logging on every Virtual Machine; references EUCS OPS-05.3H and OPS-13.1H.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The cloud platform shall encrypt data at rest and protect log integrity through immutability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall enable at-rest encryption for Storage and backups, and immutable storage for boot logs; references EUCS OPS-21.1H and OPS-13.1H.

groups.title: CLControl_Traffic Secure Traffic / Data in Transit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The cloud platform shall enforce encrypted transport and detect anomalous traffic.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall enforce TLS>=1.2, enable transport encryption (and enforcement) on Storage Services and enable anomaly detection on Network Services; references EUCS CKM-02.1B/1S and OPS-21.1H.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall operate an ISMS covering supplier relationships, cloud-service usage, ICT supply chain, personnel screening and security awareness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement processes and procedures for supplier security, cloud-service security, ICT supply-chain assurance, personnel screening and information security awareness training.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall apply a Secure Development Lifecycle to all AI and cloud components.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall apply secure architecture/engineering principles, secure coding, personnel screening and security awareness across the development lifecycle.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall control physical access to environments where AI assets are developed, trained or operated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement physical access controls, screening procedures and information security awareness for facilities hosting AI/cloud assets.

groups.title: ORControl_DevelopmentPrinciples System Architecture and Engineering Principles

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall apply secure system architecture and engineering principles to AI software and cloud components.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall document and apply secure system architecture and engineering principles across all AI and cloud subsystems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall protect the integrity of model and library supply chains used in AI development.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall validate third-party models and restrict library loading, and shall manage information security in the ICT supply chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system shall implement cryptographic mechanisms protecting data in transit and at rest.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement cryptographic mechanisms (e.g. TLS validation) covering data in transit and at rest.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system shall implement access-control mechanisms governing logical and physical access to AI and cloud assets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement access control, secure authentication and access-rights management mechanisms.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system shall implement authentication and data-authenticity mechanisms for users and integrations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The provider shall implement authentication mechanisms (e.g. SecureAuthentication metric) and authenticity controls for inputs and integrations.
